title: Create product user with email only answered 400: the server required a name the contract marks optional
summary: `POST /v1/products/{product_id}/product-users` documents `email` as the only required field, but Anchor answered 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (`field: Name, rule: required`) when `name` was left out. The domain input `CreateProductUserInput` has required `Name` since the first snapshot (2026-05-11), and the OpenAPI validator skips request bodies, so nothing compared the two rules; a CT even asserted the 400. The echopoint flow suite found it on 2026-10-26 while covering anchor#268 (`external_id`), the first test to send a product user without a name. No customer report and no log evidence of impact: validation refusals leave no trace. The fix makes `name` optional on create, as the contract says; the lesson is to send each create operation's minimum contract body once.

impact.text: Any client that followed the contract or skipped `.Name()` in the Go SDK got a 400 on product user creation, in dev and prod, for about 5.5 months. Products that are their own identity provider (anchor#268, ADR-0023) are the new callers most likely to create users without a display name. Impact on customers is unknown: 400 validation refusals are not logged with their field and rule.

numbers.label: log rows that would show a customer hitting it

trigger: The first snapshot of Anchor (98d19607, 2026-05-11) shipped `Name string validate:"required,notblank"` in `CreateProductUserInput` while the contract listed only `email` as required.
detection: The echopoint-investigation routine built `anchor: product user external id` for anchor#268 at 2026-10-26T05:13Z. Its create node sent `email` and `external_id` only and got 400 `Name is a required field`. Not sooner because every CT helper, SDK example and existing flow sends a name, and the refusal is not logged.
resolution: The flow now sends a name and the email-only check sits in `anchor: known bugs` (tag `known-bugs`, outside CI). [anchor#291](https://github.com/nanostack-dev/anchor/pull/291) makes `name` optional on create; it waits for human review because it reverses a behavior a CT pinned, so a maintainer decides whether the contract or the server is right.

whys.problem: A product creating a user with email only, as the contract allows, got 400 from Anchor

because.text: `CreateProductUserInput.Name` is `required,notblank`; the contract lists only `email` as required
Two sources state the body rules and nothing compares them: the OpenAPI validator skips request bodies
Tests assert the server's behavior, not the contract: a CT pinned the 400 that the contract forbids
because.evidence: `cmd/it/ct/product_user_create_test.go` "Creating a product user with missing name returns a bad request" asserted 400 `Name is a required field` since the first snapshot

because.text: CTs are written from the implementation; no check that each create operation accepts the minimum body its contract allows
Every test and flow that creates a product user sends a name
because.evidence: CT helper `newProductUserBody` sets `Name` from Faker; SDK examples call `.Name()`; all anchor flows send `name`

because.text: Test builders default to the fullest realistic body; the minimal request is never a named case
Test and flow conventions fill optional fields by default, with no rule to also send the contract minimum
The mismatch stayed unseen for 168 days and its customer impact cannot be measured
A 400 validation refusal leaves no log row with its operation, field and rule
because.evidence: PostHog logs, service `anchor`, last 24 h, search `Name is a required field`: 0 rows, although this run sent such requests

because.text: Client-error refusals are not counted by operation and field, so a contract-vs-server mismatch is invisible

contributing: A CT asserted the 400 with its message, so the suite defended the drift instead of catching it.
anchor#268 reviewed the new `external_id` bounds against the contract but not the neighbouring fields of the same input.
The Go SDK `Users().Create(email)` builder makes the name look optional, so an SDK caller would hit the 400 only at runtime.

well: Covering a new feature with a flow that sends only what the feature needs found an old bug in minutes.
The known-bugs flow keeps the failing check visible without blocking the CI gate.
wrong: A five-month-old contract lie went unnoticed by CTs, SDK tests and 25 anchor flows, all of which send a name.
lucky: No known customer creates product users without a name yet; ADR-0023 products (own identity provider) would have been the first.
The mismatch refused a request instead of storing bad data, so nothing needs repair.

actions.what: Make `name` optional on product user create, as the contract says; CT for the email-only body (or, if a human decides name is required, change the contract instead)
CT per create operation that sends only the contract's required properties and expects 2xx (generated from openapi.yaml)
flow-suite-testing skill + anchor testing doc: send each create's minimum contract body once
Count 400 VALIDATION_ERROR by operation, field and rule (metric or info log) and alert on a new pair

messaging.internal: Anchor answered 400 to product user creates without `name`, although the contract marks it optional (since 2026-05-11). Found by the #268 flow. Fix makes name optional; known-bugs flow tracks it until live.
messaging.external: None: no customer report and no evidence of impact.
